problem.user_text:
[R526-BATTERY declared_family=electrical source=odi:11504701 battery=R531-MEMO-COUNTERFACTUAL]

The Kia lacks engine immobilizers.  The Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard states that vehicles must  be equipped with a starting system that prevents the activation of the engine and either steering, forward mobility, or both, whenever a car's key is removed.  The purpose of the law is to decrease the likelihood that a vehicle will be stolen or accidently set in motion, and the statute applies to all passenger cars, trucks and multipurpose passenger vehicles in the country. Kia knew or had knowledge to add an engine immobilizer or similar device to the cars but failed to do so despite knowing how dangerous it was to be with the critical theft prevention measures.  My 2020 Kia is not safe and reliable and considered dangerous.  Due to insurance companies not renewing policies on Kia vehicles and the extreme decline in value of my Kia, have made my vehicle not safe, undriveable, and not reliable.   Kia falsely stated the cars are fit for their normal and intended use despite they lacked engine immobilizers at the time of sale.  All of this in violation of the law and the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard. I have a vehicle worth $12,000 less than I bought it 8 months ago and will soon not be able to insure my vehicle and will be unable to drive it.

evidence.title: The great American car crime decline.
evidence.abstract: The vehicle theft rate in the United States declined 80 percent between 1990 and 2020. Remarkably, this remains unexplained. This study examines historical evidence including reports to Congress plus automobile industry data from the Federal Register. Legislation incentivised security improvements that were fitted to high-risk vehicles from the late 1980s. Analysis of the industry data finds that theft of vehicles with electronic engine immobilizers declined 80 percent relative to a matched control group and theft of new secure vehicles declined before older vehicles. Theft declined gradually over the years as secure vehicles permeated the national vehicle fleet, the prolonged decline reflecting the arms race between manufacturers' responses and offender effort to circumvent security. The study concludes that the electronic engine immobilizer caused the great American car crime decline. If this induced declining crime more generally, the electronic engine immobilizer may be the most important crime prevention device of recent history.

mechanism_map.mechanism: Electronic engine immobilizer prevents unauthorized engine activation by requiring electronic authentication before the starting system engages.
mechanism_map.intervention: Integrate an electronic engine immobilizer module into the Kia vehicle starting system that disables engine ignition and steering column lock release unless a cryptographically authenticated key transponder is detected, satisfying FMVSS requirements.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Unauthorized engine activation and vehicle theft will be prevented when the key is removed, achieving compliance with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards for starting systems.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Attempt to start the engine and release the steering lock using a non-authenticated mechanical key blank or bypass tool; if the engine cranks or steering unlocks without valid transponder authentication, the intervention has failed.
mechanism_map.mechanism_source_span: Theft of vehicles with electronic engine immobilizers declined 80 percent relative to a matched control group

custody_records.raw_content: The vehicle theft rate in the United States declined 80 percent between 1990 and 2020. Remarkably, this remains unexplained. This study examines historical evidence including reports to Congress plus automobile industry data from the Federal Register. Legislation incentivised security improvements that were fitted to high-risk vehicles from the late 1980s. Analysis of the industry data finds that theft of vehicles with electronic engine immobilizers declined 80 percent relative to a matched control group and theft of new secure vehicles declined before older vehicles. Theft declined gradually over the years as secure vehicles permeated the national vehicle fleet, the prolonged decline reflecting the arms race between manufacturers' responses and offender effort to circumvent security. The study concludes that the electronic engine immobilizer caused the great American car crime decline. If this induced declining crime more generally, the electronic engine immobilizer may be the most important crime prevention device of recent history.
